literal: Jingmu's Twelve Sons, Part One
idiomatic: Jingmu's Twelve Sons (Part 1)

literal: Biographies 5: Jingmu's Twelve Sons, Part One
idiomatic: Biographies 5 — Jingmu's Twelve Sons (Part 1)

literal: Emperor Jingmu had fourteen sons: the Gong Empress bore Emperor Wencheng;
idiomatic: Emperor Jingmu had fourteen sons. The Gong Empress bore Emperor Wencheng;

literal: Consort Yuan of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Yangping the Somber, Xincheng;
idiomatic: Consort Yuan of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Yangping the Somber, Xincheng;

literal: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Jingzhao the Kind, Zitui, and Prince of Jiyin the Lesser, Xiaoxincheng;
idiomatic: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Jingzhao the Kind, Zitui, and the Prince of Jiyin the Lesser, Xiaoxincheng;

literal: Consort Yang of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Ruyin the Spirited, Tianci;
idiomatic: Consort Yang of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Ruyin the Spirited, Tianci;

literal: the mothers of Prince of Leliang the Stern, Wanshou, and Prince of Guangping the Untimely, Luohou are unknown.
idiomatic: the mothers of the Prince of Leliang the Stern, Wanshou, and the Prince of Guangping the Untimely, Luohou are unrecorded.

literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Rencheng the Kind, Yun;
idiomatic: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Rencheng the Kind, Yun;

literal: Consort Liu of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Nan'an the Graceful, Zhen, and Prince of Chengyang the Kind, Changshou.
idiomatic: Consort Liu of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Nan'an the Graceful, Zhen, and the Prince of Chengyang the Kind, Changshou.

literal: Consort Murong of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Zhangwu the Revered, Tailuo;
idiomatic: Consort Murong of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Zhangwu the Revered, Tailuo;

literal: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Leling the Kind, Hu'er;
idiomatic: Consort Wei of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Leling the Kind, Hu'er;

literal: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore Prince of Anding the Tranquil, Xiu.
idiomatic: Consort Meng of the Pepper Chambers bore the Prince of Anding the Tranquil, Xiu.

literal: Prince of Zhao Shen died early; no biography; mother unknown.
idiomatic: The Prince of Zhao, Shen, died in youth and has no biography; his mother is unrecorded.

literal: Under Wei custom the former crown prince's inner quarters had no rank titles; when Wencheng took the throne, palace women of Jingmu who had borne sons were all styled Pepper-Chamber consorts.
idiomatic: Under Wei custom the former crown prince's inner quarters bore no rank titles. When Wencheng took the throne, every palace woman of Jingmu who had borne a son was styled a Pepper-Chamber consort.

literal: Prince of Yangping Xincheng was enfeoffed in the third year of Tai'an and later served as Grand Palace Official of the Inner Court.
idiomatic: The Prince of Yangping, Xincheng, received his fief in the third year of Tai'an and later served as Grand Palace Official of the Inner Court.

literal: He died; posthumous title Somber.
idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Somber.

literal: His eldest son Anshou succeeded to the title; Emperor Xiaowen later granted him the name Yi.
idiomatic: His eldest son Anshou succeeded to the title; Emperor Xiaowen later granted him the name Yi.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General of Huaishuo Garrison.
idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to General of Huaishuo Garrison.

literal: As commander of the three-route armies on the northern campaign, he was summoned to the capital; the emperor exhorted him on matters of war.
idiomatic: Made commander of the three-route armies on the northern campaign, he was summoned to the capital, where the emperor exhorted him on matters of war.

literal: He replied: "I shall rely on the plans of the ancestral temple and make the Hun submit as they did at Weiqiao."
idiomatic: He replied: "I shall rely on the plans of the ancestral temple and bring the Hun to submit as they did at Weiqiao."

literal: The emperor sighed and said: "What bold words, Prince—just what I hoped to hear."
idiomatic: The emperor sighed and said: "What bold words, Prince—just what I hoped to hear."

literal: Before he set out he was struck by his mother's death; an edict sent attendants to urge him with the doctrine of metal and leather—that war does not wait for mourning—and he marched after the burial.
idiomatic: Before he set out he was struck by his mother's death. An edict sent attendants to urge him with the doctrine of metal and leather—that war does not wait for mourning—and he marched after the burial.

literal: With Lu Rui he gathered the generals of the three routes to deliberate which path the army should take.
idiomatic: With Lu Rui he gathered the generals of the three routes to decide which path the army should take.

literal: The center route went through Black Mountain, the east route toward the Shilu River, the west route toward the Houyan River.
idiomatic: The center route went through Black Mountain, the east toward the Shilu River, the west toward the Houyan River.

literal: The army crossed the great desert and routed the Rouran.
idiomatic: The army crossed the great desert and routed the Rouran.

literal: When Yi came to court, the edict said: "Your words before, Prince, have indeed proved true."
idiomatic: When Yi came to court, the edict said: "Your words before, Prince, have indeed proved true."

literal: Later he was made governor of Shuozhou.
idiomatic: Later he was made governor of Shuozhou.

literal: When Governor of Hengzhou Mu Tai plotted rebellion, he sent envoys urging Yi as leader; Yi secretly reported the matter.
idiomatic: When the governor of Hengzhou, Mu Tai, plotted rebellion, he sent envoys urging Yi to lead them; Yi secretly reported the matter.

literal: Tai and the rest were executed; the emperor greatly praised him.
idiomatic: Tai and his accomplices were executed; the emperor greatly praised him.

literal: In the first year of Jingming under Emperor Xuanwu he died as governor of Qingzhou; posthumous title Prince Zhuang.
idiomatic: In the first year of Jingming under Emperor Xuanwu he died in office as governor of Qingzhou and was given the posthumous title Prince Zhuang.

literal: The fief passed to his grandson Zongyin.
idiomatic: The fief passed to his grandson Zongyin.

literal: Under Emperor Ming he was sentenced to death for killing his uncle; the title was extinguished.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was sentenced to death for killing his uncle; the title was extinguished.

literal: Yi's younger brother Yan, styled Anle, was granted the title Marquis of Guangling and made governor of Liangzhou.
idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Yan, styled Anle, was granted the title Marquis of Guangling and made governor of Liangzhou.

literal: He memorialized asking for a provisional kingship to enhance his authority.
idiomatic: He memorialized asking for a provisional kingship to enhance his authority.

literal: The edict said: "This may be called insatiable ambition; the request is not granted."
idiomatic: The edict said: "This may be called insatiable ambition; the request is not granted."

literal: He was transferred to governor of Xuzhou.
idiomatic: He was transferred to governor of Xuzhou.

literal: On reaching the province he fell gravely ill; the emperor ordered Xu Chengbai to ride post-haste to treat him.
idiomatic: On reaching the province he fell gravely ill; the emperor ordered Xu Chengbai to ride post-haste to treat him.

literal: When he recovered, Chengbai returned.
idiomatic: When he recovered, Chengbai returned.

literal: The emperor said: "You are truly a famous physician."
idiomatic: The emperor said: "You are truly a famous physician."

literal: He was rewarded with three thousand bolts of silk.
idiomatic: He was rewarded with three thousand bolts of silk.

literal: Chengbai declined and asked to accept only one thousand.
idiomatic: Chengbai declined and asked to accept only one thousand.

literal: The emperor said: "The Odes says: 'When men of worth perish, the state is laid waste.'"
idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Odes says: 'When men of worth perish, the state is laid waste.'"

literal: By that reckoning, is three thousand bolts the limit?
idiomatic: By that reckoning, is three thousand bolts the limit?

literal: Such was the esteem in which the emperor held him.
idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which the emperor held him.

literal: Later his birth mother Lady Lei died; he memorialized asking to resign the province.
idiomatic: Later his birth mother, Lady Lei, died; he memorialized asking to resign the province.

literal: The edict said: "The displeasure felt toward a former ruler's lesser consorts is explicit in the Rites."
idiomatic: The edict said: "The displeasure felt toward a former ruler's lesser consorts is explicit in the Rites."

literal: In the decline of the age that canon has sometimes fallen into disuse.
idiomatic: In the decline of the age that canon has sometimes fallen into disuse.

literal: As the son of an imperial prince you should follow the rule of lesser consorts and may observe the greater mourning.
idiomatic: As the son of an imperial prince you should follow the rule of lesser consorts and may observe the greater mourning.

literal: Later he died as governor of Yongzhou; posthumous title Marquis Kang.
idiomatic: Later he died in office as governor of Yongzhou and was given the posthumous title Marquis Kang.

literal: Yan was by nature cautious and pure; wherever he served he was incorrupt, kept no estates, and through four provinces left a name for achievement—yet on the day he died there was not even a shroud for his corpse.
idiomatic: Yan was by nature cautious and pure. Wherever he served he was incorrupt, kept no estates, and through four provinces left a name for achievement—yet on the day he died there was not even a shroud for his corpse.

literal: His son Chang, styled Shuchang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and enfeoffed Prince of Boling.
idiomatic: His son Chang, styled Shuchang, followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong and was made Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception and enfeoffed as Prince of Boling.

literal: In the third year of Datong he campaigned east and fell in battle.
idiomatic: In the third year of Datong he campaigned east and fell in battle.

literal: His son Min was addicted to wine and extravagant spending; the household was ruined by it.
idiomatic: His son Min was addicted to wine and extravagant spending; the household was ruined by it.

literal: His sons-in-law, pillar of state Yifu Gui and great general Dali Ji You, each had wealth in the tens of millions and supplied him whenever he asked.
idiomatic: His sons-in-law, the pillar of state Yifu Gui and the great general Dali Ji You, each had wealth in the tens of millions and supplied him whenever he asked.

literal: Min would scatter it all at once, yet the emperor did not reproach him.
idiomatic: Min would scatter it all at once, yet the emperor did not reproach him.

literal: Gui and You eventually cut him off.
idiomatic: Gui and You eventually cut him off.

literal: He held the rank Pillar of State, third grade; his fief was changed to Duke of Nanwu County.
idiomatic: He held the rank of Pillar of State, third grade; his fief was changed to Duke of Nanwu County.

literal: Chang's younger brother Rong, styled Shurong, was very short and ugly in appearance yet surpassingly fierce in battle.
idiomatic: Chang's younger brother Rong, styled Shurong, was very short and ugly in appearance yet surpassingly fierce in battle.

literal: When Emperor Zhuangdi plotted to kill Erzhu Rong, Rong was made a direct-gate general.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangdi plotted to kill Erzhu Rong, Rong was made a direct-gate general.

literal: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Rong fled among the people.
idiomatic: When Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang, Rong fled among the people.

literal: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, was enfeoffed Prince of Weixing, and held the posts of Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.
idiomatic: Later he followed Emperor Xiaowu into Guanzhong, was enfeoffed Prince of Weixing, and held the posts of Attendant and Director of the Palace Secretariat.

literal: Yan's younger brother Qin, styled Siruo, held the posts of Director of the Secretariat, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Pillar of State, third grade.
idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Qin, styled Siruo, held the posts of Director of the Secretariat, Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Pillar of State, third grade.

literal: Qin's complexion was especially dark, so people of the time called him the Black-Faced Vice Director.
idiomatic: Qin's complexion was especially dark, so people of the time called him the Black-Faced Vice Director.

literal: Qin debauched his cousin Li's wife, the Lady Cui; Censor-in-Chief Feng Hui impeached him, but he was pardoned.
idiomatic: Qin debauched his cousin Li's wife, the Lady Cui; the censor-in-chief Feng Hui impeached him, but he was pardoned.

literal: Soon after he was made governor of Sizhou.
idiomatic: Soon after he was made governor of Sizhou.

literal: Qin loved learning from youth and had an early reputation.
idiomatic: Qin loved learning from youth and had an early reputation.

literal: People of the time said: "Among the imperial clan, briefly—Shou'an and Siruo."
idiomatic: People of the time said: "Among the imperial clan, briefly—Shou'an and Siruo."

literal: When in later years he grew eminent he could no longer offer useful counsel; critics looked down on him.
idiomatic: When in later years he grew eminent he could no longer offer useful counsel; critics looked down on him.

literal: Qin once asked the man of Qingzhou, the monk Gaosengshou, to find a tutor for his son; the tutor arrived but fled after only a few days.
idiomatic: Qin once asked the man of Qingzhou, the monk Gaosengshou, to find a tutor for his son; the tutor arrived but fled after only a few days.

literal: Qin reproached Gaosengshou.
idiomatic: Qin reproached Gaosengshou.

literal: Gaosengshou, a man of wit, retorted to Qin: "An ordinary man dies after seven days without grain; this one lasted barely five mornings before fleeing—abandoning food for faith, he plainly lacked something."
idiomatic: Gaosengshou, a man of wit, retorted to Qin: "An ordinary man dies after seven days without grain; this one lasted barely five mornings before fleeing—abandoning food for faith, he plainly lacked something."

literal: Qin was deeply ashamed and thereafter treated guests somewhat more generously.
idiomatic: Qin was deeply ashamed and thereafter treated guests somewhat more generously.

literal: Later he was made Duke of the State and enfeoffed Duke of Juping County.
idiomatic: Later he was made Duke of the State and enfeoffed as Duke of Juping County.

literal: He was killed at Heyin; posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Duke.
idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin and posthumously given the golden axe, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Duke.

literal: His son Zixiao, styled Jiye, had an early reputation.
idiomatic: His son Zixiao, styled Jiye, had an early reputation.

literal: At eight years old, Director of the Secretariat Cui Guang saw him and marveled, saying: "The leader of the coming generation will surely be this boy."
idiomatic: At eight years old, Director of the Secretariat Cui Guang saw him and marveled, saying: "The leader of the coming generation will surely be this boy."

literal: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong he did not manage to follow the imperial carriage.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu entered Guanzhong he did not manage to follow the imperial carriage.

literal: Later he went to Chang'an and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang.
idiomatic: Later he went to Chang'an and was enfeoffed Prince of Yiyang.

literal: Zixiao was handsome, skilled at jest and banter, loved wine and honored scholars; the gentry flocked to him, his hall always full of guests, and he never tired of it.
idiomatic: Zixiao was handsome, skilled at jest and banter, loved wine and honored scholars; the gentry flocked to him, his hall always full of guests, and he never tired of it.

literal: His nature was also generous and kind; he treated his kinsmen with warmth and respect.
idiomatic: His nature was also generous and kind; he treated his kinsmen with warmth and respect.

literal: He established a school in his private residence and gathered younger kinsmen to lecture day and night.
idiomatic: He established a school in his private residence and gathered younger kinsmen to lecture day and night.

literal: He provided food and clothing and treated them as his own sons.
idiomatic: He provided food and clothing and treated them as his own sons.

literal: Later he served as Director of the Secretariat and Pillar of State, great general.
idiomatic: Later he served as Director of the Secretariat and as Pillar of State, great general.

literal: Zixiao saw the dynasty's fortune slipping away and humbled himself deeply, drinking day and night.
idiomatic: Zixiao saw the dynasty's fortune slipping away and humbled himself deeply, drinking day and night.

literal: Later by precedent he was reduced to duke and restored the surname Tuoba.
idiomatic: Later by precedent he was reduced to duke and restored the surname Tuoba.

literal: Before long he died; his son Yun succeeded.
idiomatic: Before long he died; his son Yun succeeded.

literal: Yun's son Taixing succeeded and was made General of Chang'an Garrison.
idiomatic: Yun's son Taixing succeeded and was made General of Chang'an Garrison.

literal: For corruption he was stripped of office and rank.
idiomatic: For corruption he was stripped of office and rank.

literal: Later he was made Director of the Secretariat, restored to his former title, and his fief changed to Xihé.
idiomatic: Later he was made Director of the Secretariat, restored to his former title, and his fief changed to Xihé.

literal: He was transferred to Commandant of the Palace Guard.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Commandant of the Palace Guard.

literal: At first, when Taixing fell ill, he asked monks to perform rites for him.
idiomatic: At first, when Taixing fell ill, he asked monks to perform rites for him.

literal: All his possessions were given away at once in a distribution called the Liberation Fast, begging recovery from illness.
idiomatic: All his possessions were given away at once in a distribution called the Liberation Fast, begging recovery from illness.

literal: After the fast the monks scattered in all directions; one monk was still asking for leftover food from the fast.
idiomatic: After the fast the monks scattered in all directions; one monk was still asking for leftover food from the fast.

literal: Taixing jested with him:
idiomatic: Taixing jested with him:

literal: "The fast food is gone; only wine and meat remain."
idiomatic: "The fast food is gone; only wine and meat remain."

literal: The monk said: "I can eat those too."
idiomatic: The monk said: "I can eat those too."

literal: So he brought out a dou of wine and a leg of mutton.
idiomatic: So he brought out a dou of wine and a leg of mutton.

literal: When he had finished eating he still said he was not full.
idiomatic: When he had finished eating he still said he was not full.

literal: After he left, the wine and meat were still there.
idiomatic: After he left, the wine and meat were still there.

literal: Going out the gate to pursue him, he was nowhere to be seen.
idiomatic: Going out the gate to pursue him, he was nowhere to be seen.
